quests.hint: The reply to 'thank you' in a polite phrase.
quests.explanation: 'You're welcome' is the standard neutral reply to thanks. More casual options are 'No problem' and 'Anytime'; a warmer one is 'My pleasure'.
quests.textToSpeak: When people thank me, I usually just say 'You're ___'.
quests.correctAnswer: When people thank me, I usually just say 'You're welcome'.
quests.contextClue: The phrase answers being thanked.

quests.hint: A polite word used to ask someone to repeat.
quests.explanation: 'I beg your pardon?' is a polite, slightly formal way to ask someone to repeat. 'Sorry?' or 'Pardon?' is more common in everyday speech.
quests.textToSpeak: He leaned forward and asked, 'I beg your ___?' because he hadn't caught my name.
quests.correctAnswer: He leaned forward and asked, 'I beg your pardon?' because he hadn't caught my name.
quests.contextClue: Not catching a name leads to a polite request to repeat.

quests.hint: A polite way to leave a conversation briefly.
quests.explanation: 'Excuse me' is a polite way to interrupt or step away. 'Please excuse me' sounds a little more formal than 'Sorry, I have to take this'.
quests.textToSpeak: Please ___ me for a moment; I need to take this call.
quests.correctAnswer: Please excuse me for a moment; I need to take this call.
quests.contextClue: A phone call requires leaving briefly.

quests.hint: An extreme, informal way of saying you need food right now.
quests.explanation: 'Starving' is an informal exaggeration for very hungry. Extreme adjectives like this go with 'absolutely', not 'very'.
quests.textToSpeak: Let's order pizza now. I'm absolutely ___!
quests.correctAnswer: Let's order pizza now. I'm absolutely starving!
quests.contextClue: Wanting to order immediately shows how strongly the speaker feels.

quests.hint: Accepted ways of behaving politely.
quests.explanation: 'Bad manners' means impolite behaviour; 'good manners' is the opposite. Manners is always plural in this meaning.
quests.textToSpeak: It's bad ___ to talk with your mouth full, especially at someone else's table.
quests.correctAnswer: It's bad manners to talk with your mouth full, especially at someone else's table.
quests.contextClue: Rules for behaviour at a table.

quests.hint: Showing respect for others in the way you speak.
quests.explanation: A polite request often uses 'Could you...?' or 'Would you...?'. Commands with no softening sound rude.
quests.textToSpeak: It sounds more ___ to say 'Could you pass the salt?' than 'Give me the salt.'
quests.correctAnswer: It sounds more polite to say 'Could you pass the salt?' than 'Give me the salt.'
quests.contextClue: Two requests are compared by how respectful they sound.

quests.hint: Give part of your work to other people.
quests.explanation: 'Delegate' means give a task or authority to someone else. It is common in management language: 'delegate tasks to the team'.
quests.textToSpeak: I can't do everything myself, so I'll ___ some of the tasks to the team.
quests.correctAnswer: I can't do everything myself, so I'll delegate some of the tasks to the team.
quests.contextClue: Overload leads to sharing tasks.

quests.hint: Add someone as a recipient of an email.
quests.explanation: 'Copy someone in' means include them on an email. It comes from 'cc', which stands for 'carbon copy'.
quests.textToSpeak: Please ___ me in on the reply so that I can follow the discussion.
quests.correctAnswer: Please copy me in on the reply so that I can follow the discussion.
quests.contextClue: Following a discussion requires receiving the emails.

quests.hint: An early version of a piece of writing.
quests.explanation: A 'draft' is an early version of a text, before the final one. We 'write', 'send' or 'revise' a draft.
quests.textToSpeak: I've written the first ___ of the proposal; could you take a look?
quests.correctAnswer: I've written the first draft of the proposal; could you take a look?
quests.contextClue: 'First' and 'take a look' suggest an unfinished text.

quests.hint: Feeling thankful for a favour.
quests.explanation: 'We would be grateful if you could...' is a polite formal request. It sounds more formal than 'Can you...?'
quests.textToSpeak: We would be ___ if you could confirm your attendance by Friday.
quests.correctAnswer: We would be grateful if you could confirm your attendance by Friday.
quests.contextClue: A request to confirm by a date is framed politely.

quests.hint: A polite word in the closing line of an email.
quests.explanation: 'Kind regards' and 'Best regards' are neutral, professional email sign-offs. Casual ones include 'Thanks' or 'Cheers'.
quests.textToSpeak: I always end my work emails with 'Kind ___,' followed by my name.
quests.correctAnswer: I always end my work emails with 'Kind regards,' followed by my name.
quests.contextClue: The word appears in a sign-off before the name.

quests.hint: Obliged to do something by a rule.
quests.explanation: 'Be required to + verb' is a formal way of saying a rule obliges you. In casual talk we say 'You need to...' or 'You have to...'.
quests.textToSpeak: Applicants are ___ to provide two references with their form.
quests.correctAnswer: Applicants are required to provide two references with their form.
quests.contextClue: A rule for applicants signals a formal obligation.

quests.hint: The goods a shop has available to sell.
quests.explanation: 'Out of stock' means a shop has none left. The opposite is 'in stock'. It is standard customer-service language.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm afraid that model is currently out of ___.
quests.correctAnswer: I'm afraid that model is currently out of stock.
quests.contextClue: A shop cannot sell an item it doesn't have.

quests.hint: The ability to wait calmly.
quests.explanation: 'Thank you for your patience' is a standard customer-service phrase. It thanks people for waiting without complaining.
quests.textToSpeak: Thank you for your ___ while we resolve this issue.
quests.correctAnswer: Thank you for your patience while we resolve this issue.
quests.contextClue: A problem is being fixed, and the customer is waiting.

quests.hint: A small problem or trouble caused to someone.
quests.explanation: 'Inconvenience' is the formal word for a small problem someone has because of a change. 'Sorry for the trouble' is the everyday version.
quests.textToSpeak: We apologise for any ___ this may have caused.
quests.correctAnswer: We apologise for any inconvenience this may have caused.
quests.contextClue: An apology is offered for a minor problem.

quests.hint: An adverb meaning honestly, used to close a letter.
quests.explanation: In British style, 'Yours sincerely' is used when you know the person's name. 'Yours faithfully' is used with 'Dear Sir or Madam'.
quests.textToSpeak: I know the manager's name is Mr Adams, so I'll end the letter with 'Yours ___'.
quests.correctAnswer: I know the manager's name is Mr Adams, so I'll end the letter with 'Yours sincerely'.
quests.contextClue: A named recipient decides which closing to use.

quests.hint: Placed inside the same envelope as the letter.
quests.explanation: 'Enclosed' is used for things in a paper letter's envelope. For emails we say 'attached'.
quests.textToSpeak: I've put a copy of the receipt in the envelope, so please find it ___.
quests.correctAnswer: I've put a copy of the receipt in the envelope, so please find it enclosed.
quests.contextClue: An envelope suggests a paper letter.

quests.hint: Politely say no.
quests.explanation: 'Decline' is a formal, polite way to say no to an offer or invitation. 'Turn down' is more casual.
quests.textToSpeak: Thank you for the offer, but I must respectfully ___.
quests.correctAnswer: Thank you for the offer, but I must respectfully decline.
quests.contextClue: 'Respectfully' and 'offer' point to a formal refusal.

quests.hint: An adverb that makes an order sound polite.
quests.explanation: 'Kindly requested' is common in official notices. It sounds formal, and can also sound slightly firm.
quests.textToSpeak: Passengers are ___ requested to keep their belongings with them at all times.
quests.correctAnswer: Passengers are kindly requested to keep their belongings with them at all times.
quests.contextClue: An official notice to passengers.

quests.hint: The plural noun for saying sorry formally.
quests.explanation: 'Please accept our apologies' is a formal way to say sorry. The plural form is standard in this phrase.
quests.textToSpeak: Please accept our sincere ___ for the error on your bill.
quests.correctAnswer: Please accept our sincere apologies for the error on your bill.
quests.contextClue: A company writes to a customer about a mistake.

quests.hint: Give someone official information.
quests.explanation: 'Inform' is the formal verb for telling someone information: 'We regret to inform you...'. 'Tell' is the everyday word.
quests.textToSpeak: We regret to ___ you that your application was unsuccessful.
quests.correctAnswer: We regret to inform you that your application was unsuccessful.
quests.contextClue: Bad news in a formal letter.

quests.hint: Value something someone did for you.
quests.explanation: 'I really appreciate it' is a warm, neutral way to show thanks. It works in both casual and professional settings.
quests.textToSpeak: I really ___ your help with the move; I couldn't have done it alone.
quests.correctAnswer: I really appreciate your help with the move; I couldn't have done it alone.
quests.contextClue: 'Couldn't have done it alone' shows gratitude.

quests.hint: The noun for a request to come to an event.
quests.explanation: 'Invitation' is the noun; 'invite' is the verb and, informally, also a noun. 'Kind invitation' is a formal-sounding response.
quests.textToSpeak: Thank you for your kind ___ to the wedding; we would be honoured to attend.
quests.correctAnswer: Thank you for your kind invitation to the wedding; we would be honoured to attend.
quests.contextClue: A formal reply to a wedding request.

quests.hint: A polite message declining an invitation.
quests.explanation: 'Send your regrets' means say you cannot come, in a formal way. The plural is the fixed form.
quests.textToSpeak: Please send your ___ if you are unable to attend the dinner.
quests.correctAnswer: Please send your regrets if you are unable to attend the dinner.
quests.contextClue: An invitation needs a reply if the guest cannot come.

quests.hint: Requiring serious clothes and behaviour.
quests.explanation: 'Formal' describes serious situations, dress or language. The opposite is 'informal' or 'casual'.
quests.textToSpeak: The invitation says black tie, so it's a very ___ occasion.
quests.correctAnswer: The invitation says black tie, so it's a very formal occasion.
quests.contextClue: Black tie shows a serious event.

quests.hint: Relaxed and informal.
quests.explanation: 'Casual' describes relaxed clothes or events. Its opposite is 'formal'.
quests.textToSpeak: Don't worry about a suit; it's a ___ get-together with the team.
quests.correctAnswer: Don't worry about a suit; it's a casual get-together with the team.
quests.contextClue: A team get-together with no suit suggests a relaxed event.

quests.hint: Careful not to upset people with what you say.
quests.explanation: 'Tactful' describes saying difficult things without offending. The noun is 'tact'.
quests.textToSpeak: He was very ___ about it and chose his words carefully.
quests.correctAnswer: He was very tactful about it and chose his words carefully.
quests.contextClue: Choosing words carefully points to a sensitive approach.

quests.hint: An adverb used to close a letter to an unnamed person.
quests.explanation: In British style, 'Yours faithfully' goes with 'Dear Sir or Madam'. 'Yours sincerely' goes with a name.
quests.textToSpeak: I began with 'Dear Sir or Madam', so I must end with 'Yours ___'.
quests.correctAnswer: I began with 'Dear Sir or Madam', so I must end with 'Yours faithfully'.
quests.contextClue: An unnamed recipient decides the closing.

quests.hint: Polite behaviour toward others.
quests.explanation: 'As a matter of courtesy' means as a polite thing to do, not because of a rule. It is neutral to formal.
quests.textToSpeak: As a matter of ___, please tell the front desk if you plan to leave early.
quests.correctAnswer: As a matter of courtesy, please tell the front desk if you plan to leave early.
quests.contextClue: The request is polite rather than mandatory.

quests.hint: The accepted rules for behaving properly in a situation.
quests.explanation: 'Etiquette' means the accepted rules for behaviour in a particular setting. We say 'business etiquette' or 'table etiquette'.
quests.textToSpeak: Business ___ varies across countries, so it helps to read about local customs first.
quests.correctAnswer: Business etiquette varies across countries, so it helps to read about local customs first.
quests.contextClue: Reading about local customs is preparation for correct behaviour.
